question: Using the inverse-matrix method, solve $2x+y=5$ and $x-y=1$.
explanation:
Step 1: Write the matrix equation
The system can be written as $$AX=B,$$ where $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix},\quad X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}5\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 2: Find the inverse
Since $|A|=-3\ne0$, $$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{-3}\begin{bmatrix}-1&-1\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{3}&\frac{1}{3}\\\frac{1}{3}&-\frac{2}{3}\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 3: Calculate $X$
Using $X=A^{-1}B$, $$X=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{1}{3}&\frac{1}{3}\\\frac{1}{3}&-\frac{2}{3}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}5\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 4: State the solution
Hence, $x=2$ and $y=1$.
